title: Child Nutrition & Healthy Feeding
source: ICMR, National Health Mission, UNICEF India

chunks.title: First 6 Months - Exclusive Breastfeeding
chunks.content: Breast milk is BEST food for 0-6 month baby - NO water, NO formula needed. Breastfeeding benefits: transfers immunity, prevents infections (diarrhea, pneumonia, ear infections), prevents malnutrition, creates bonding. Mother's first milk (colostrum) is yellow thick liquid - DO NOT discard, it has antibodies. Breastfeed on-demand (8-12 times/day). Signs of good feeding: baby drinks for 10-15 min per breast, makes swallowing sounds, 6+ wet diapers daily, steady weight gain. Mother needs extra 500 calories/day - eat nutritious food.

chunks.title: Complementary Feeding - 6-24 Months
chunks.content: At 6 months, start complementary foods while continuing breastfeeding. Start with iron-rich foods: soft cooked rice with lentils (dal), fortified cereal, egg (yolk first), meat/chicken (ground). Introduce one new food every 3 days - watch for allergies (rash, vomiting, diarrhea). By 8 months: Mash foods (avoid choking hazard like whole nuts, grapes). By 12 months: Family food (without excess salt/spices). Continue breastfeeding until 2 years. By 24 months, child should eat 3 meals + 1-2 snacks matching family diet (soft, no whole nuts).

chunks.title: Prevention of Stunting & Malnutrition
chunks.content: Stunting (short height for age) affects 1 in 3 Indian children - caused by chronic malnutrition. Prevent by: (1) Exclusive breastfeeding until 6 months, (2) Nutritious weaning foods from 6 months, (3) Home fortification - add 1 iron+vitamin D spoon (Fortified Rice Kernel) to rice, (4) Egg 4-5 times weekly (affordable protein), (5) Local vegetables/greens, (6) Deworming at 12-24 months (given free at health center), (7) Growing height measurement at health check-ups. Nutrition in first 1000 days (conception to 2 years) determines lifetime health.

chunks.title: Anemia Prevention in Women & Children
chunks.content: Anemia (low blood) affects 50%+ women/girls in India. Causes: iron deficiency, malnutrition, heavy periods, pregnancy. Symptoms: tiredness, pale skin/nails, breathlessness, dizziness. Prevent: Eat iron-rich foods (leafy greens-spinach, dal, meat, jaggery), take iron tablet if prescribed by health worker. Iron tablet color may turn stool black - this is normal. Pregnant women get iron supplements free - take daily. Children 6-59 months get iron syrup free. Vitamin C helps iron absorption (eat citrus fruit with iron meals).

chunks.title: Maternal Nutrition During Pregnancy & Lactation
chunks.content: Pregnant women need extra 350 calories/day + protein, iron, calcium, folic acid. Eat: dal (protein+iron), leafy vegetables (iron+folate), egg, milk, local seasonal fruits. Avoid: uncooked meat (listeria risk), raw eggs, unpasteurized milk, excess caffeine. Take iron+calcium supplements given free at health center. Take folic acid tablet (prevents birth defects) - most critical in first 3 months. Lactating mothers need extra 500 calories/day - continue nutritious diet. Water intake is important - drink 8-10 glasses daily. Avoid alcohol, smoking, excess spices during lactation.
